note: Plain meanings for the words people trip over. Shown when you hover a dotted word. One or two sentences each, no jargon in the explanation.

terms.DPIA: A data protection impact assessment. A written check of what could go wrong for people, and what you'll do about it, before you start.
terms.screening: A short set of questions that says whether you need a full DPIA. The canvas answers them from your picture.
terms.DPA: A data protection agreement. The contract that says a company will only use your data the way you tell it to, and keep it safe.
terms.Article 28: The part of the law that lists what a DPA must contain. Nine terms, like 'only acts on your instructions' and 'deletes the data at the end'.
terms.controller: The organisation that decides why and how data is used. Usually you.
terms.processor: A company that handles data for you, only on your instructions. Microsoft running Copilot for your college is one.
terms.sub-processor: A company your supplier uses behind the scenes. Your supplier needs your permission to use it.
terms.joint controller: Another organisation that decides with you why and how the data is used. You need a sharing agreement, not a DPA.
terms.special category: The most sensitive data: health, ethnicity, religion, sexuality, union membership, biometrics, genetics. Crime data is treated the same way.
terms.pseudonymised: Names swapped for a code, with the list that links codes to names kept somewhere else. Still personal data, but much safer.
terms.anonymised: Nobody can work out who it's about, even with other information. It stops being personal data.
terms.lawful basis: The legal reason you're allowed to use the data. For schools and colleges it's usually 'public task': it's part of your job.
terms.privacy notice: The document that tells people what you do with their data. It needs a line for anything new, like using AI.
terms.RoPA: Record of processing activities. The organisation's list of everything it does with personal data.
terms.tier: How sensitive the data is, from 0 (nothing personal) to 3 (the most sensitive). The tier decides which tools you may use.
terms.sanctioned route: A tool or company your organisation has already approved for a given tier.
terms.DPO: The data protection officer. The person who signs off anything risky and can answer questions.
